title: Singleton Fourier sum bounded by majority
statement: Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, interpreted as real-valued by its sign. The absolute value of the sum of its degree-one Fourier coefficients is at most the sum of the degree-one Fourier coefficients of the majority function, which outputs the sign of the sum of the input coordinates (with zero assigned the positive sign).
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function from the sign cube of dimension $n$ to the signs
